heading: [BRITAIN'S SECRETARY OF STATE FOR WAR](orange) WAS SHARING A [MISTRESS](red) WITH A [SOVIET NAVAL OFFICER](orange).
body: In **1963**, [John Profumo](orange) — [UK Secretary of State for War](orange), with access to [NATO](orange) nuclear defence briefings — was revealed to have been involved with [Christine Keeler](orange), a young woman who was simultaneously involved with [Captain Yevgeny Ivanov](orange), a [Soviet Naval Intelligence](orange) attaché. The extent of any information passed between the relationships was never fully established in [court](orange). [Profumo](orange) lied to the [House of Commons](orange) about his involvement, later admitted it, and resigned. The scandal severely damaged the [Macmillan government](orange) and contributed to the [Conservative Party's](orange) election loss in **1964**.
photo_prompt: 1960s London club interior, suited figures in elegant surroundings, champagne glasses, Cold War-era glamour meets intelligence risk, documentary social photography, amber evening light

heading: [THREE COMPANIES](orange) LEGALLY SHIPPED [76 BILLION OPIOID PILLS](red) TO 9 STATES. THEY WERE REQUIRED TO FLAG [SUSPICIOUS ORDERS](red).
body: [McKesson](orange), [AmerisourceBergen](orange), and [Cardinal Health](orange) are the three largest pharmaceutical distributors in the US. Between **2006 and 2016**, they shipped **76 billion opioid pills** to [West Virginia, Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, Ohio, Alabama, Arkansas, Utah, and Nevada](orange). Under [DEA](orange) regulations, distributors are legally required to [report and refuse suspicious orders](red) — orders that appear to exceed what any pharmacy could legitimately dispense. The distributors [repeatedly failed to do so](red). In **2022**, all three agreed to pay a combined **$21 billion** to settle state and local lawsuits.
photo_prompt: Pharmaceutical distribution warehouse interior, rows of white pill bottles on conveyor belts, clinical cold lighting, the industrial scale of drug distribution made visible

heading: AN 8-STOREY FACTORY [COLLAPSED](red) IN 2013. [1,132 WORKERS DIED](red) MAKING [WESTERN FASHION](orange).
body: On **April 23, 2013**, structural cracks were discovered in the [Rana Plaza](orange) building in [Dhaka, Bangladesh](orange). Banks and shops on lower floors **closed for safety reasons**. [Garment workers on upper floors were told to return to work anyway](red) — suppliers reportedly faced penalties for missed delivery deadlines. On **April 24th**, the **8-storey building collapsed**. [1,132 people were killed](red). At least **2,500 were injured**. The building housed factories supplying clothes to [Primark](orange), [Mango](orange), [Walmart](orange), and other Western retailers. The [Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety](orange) was created in direct response.
photo_prompt: Textile factory workers at sewing machines in a densely packed floor, overhead fluorescent lighting, documentary photojournalism aesthetic, the human scale of fast fashion production

heading: THE [CIA](orange) AND [SOVIET KGB](orange) WERE SIMULTANEOUSLY FUNDING OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE SAME [CIVIL WAR](red) IN AFRICA.
body: When [Angola](orange) became independent from [Portugal](orange) in **November 1975**, three competing factions immediately fought for control. The [CIA](orange) covertly funded and armed the [FNLA](orange) and [UNITA](orange) factions under **Operation FEATURE**. The [Soviet Union](orange) funded the [MPLA](orange) and arranged for [Cuban troops](orange) to deploy. [Congress](orange) passed the **Clark Amendment** in **1975** specifically prohibiting [US military involvement in Angola](orange) after the operation became known. Declassified documents show the [CIA](orange) had deployed **$32 million** and the [KGB](orange) had deployed significant support — both [without the knowledge of most of their own governments' citizens](red).
photo_prompt: 1970s African savannah landscape with military equipment barely visible in the background, documentary Cold War military photography, dry landscape, distant conflict

heading: THE [NFL](orange) FUNDED ITS OWN [CONCUSSION](red) RESEARCH. IT [DENIED CTE EVIDENCE](red). INTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS TOLD A DIFFERENT STORY.
body: From **1994 to 2009**, the [NFL](orange) ran its own **Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Committee**, which [repeatedly published research denying a link between football and long-term brain damage](red), despite [neuropathologist Dr. Bennet Omalu](orange) publishing peer-reviewed research in **2005** linking football to [Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE)](orange). Internal [House of Representatives](orange) correspondence revealed in **2009** showed [NFL](orange) officials were [aware of CTE risks while publicly disputing them](red). The [NFL](orange) settled a class-action lawsuit with **20,000 former players** for **$1 billion** in **2015**, without admitting liability.
photo_prompt: Football helmet in extreme close-up, a single crack in the shell visible, dark background, stark documentary product photography, the visible and invisible damage of contact sport

heading: "[KILL THE INDIAN](red), SAVE THE MAN" — THE [US GOVERNMENT'S](orange) OFFICIAL APPROACH TO [NATIVE AMERICAN CHILDREN](orange).
body: [Carlisle Indian Industrial School](orange) in [Pennsylvania](orange) was founded in **1879** by [Captain Richard Henry Pratt](orange), who coined the phrase: **"Kill the Indian in him, and save the man."** The school — funded by the [US federal government](orange) — was the model for a nationwide network of **408 boarding schools** that forcibly separated [Native American](orange) children from their families, [banned Indigenous languages and ceremonies](red), and forced assimilation through English education and Christian religion. A **2022 US Interior Department report** documented [53 burial sites near these schools](red) and confirmed [children died in the schools](red) and were buried far from their families.

heading: THE [WHITE HOUSE](orange) SOLD [ARMS TO IRAN](red) UNDER AN EMBARGO. FUNNELED THE MONEY TO REBEL FIGHTERS. THEN [SHREDDED](red) THE DOCUMENTS.
body: In **1986**, it was revealed that senior [White House](orange) officials — including [National Security Council](orange) aide [Oliver North](orange) — had secretly sold [weapons to Iran](red), which was under a **US arms embargo**, and [diverted the profits to fund Contra rebels in Nicaragua](red) — a funding mechanism [Congress](orange) had explicitly prohibited. When investigators arrived, [North](orange) and his secretary [shredded thousands of documents](red). [North](orange) was convicted on **three counts** in **1989** but the convictions were vacated on appeal due to immunity deals. [President Reagan](orange) said he had no knowledge of the diversion. **11 officials were convicted**, and **6 were later pardoned** by [President George H.W. Bush](orange).
photo_prompt: 1986 White House situation room, a shredder visible in one corner, classified documents on a table, dramatic late-night office lighting, documentary political crisis photography

heading: [NAVIENT](orange) WAS PAID TO HELP STUDENT LOAN BORROWERS. IT WAS [STEERING THEM](red) INTO [MORE EXPENSIVE OPTIONS](red) INSTEAD.
body: [Navient](orange) — spun off from [Sallie Mae](orange) in **2014** — serviced **$300 billion** in federal and private student loans for **12 million borrowers**. In **2017**, the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](orange) sued [Navient](orange), alleging it [systematically steered borrowers away from income-driven repayment programmes](red) — which would have lowered monthly payments — and into [forbearance plans that cost more long-term](red), because the processing was simpler for the company. In **2022**, [Navient](orange) reached a **$1.85 billion settlement** with **39 state attorneys general** and cancelled **$1.7 billion in private student loans**. [Navient](orange) did not admit wrongdoing.
photo_prompt: Stack of student loan documents on a desk beside a university diploma, dramatic spotlight, the debt burden visualised through paper, documentary financial photography

heading: [US SOLDIERS](orange) WERE ORDERED TO [WATCH NUCLEAR BOMB TESTS](red) FROM TRENCHES. THEN TOLD [NEVER TO SPEAK OF IT](red).
body: Between **1945 and 1963**, approximately **400,000 US military personnel** were present at nuclear tests in [Nevada](orange), the [Pacific](orange), and [elsewhere](orange) — often positioned in [trenches a few miles from detonation sites](red) to test how infantry could operate after nuclear exchange. Many were ordered to [march into the blast area immediately after detonation](red). They were told radiation exposure was minimal. Veterans later reported [unusually high rates of cancer](red). Many were told under the **Atomic Energy Act** they [could face prosecution for discussing their exposure](red). Congress only formally recognised these veterans and created a compensation programme in **1988**.
photo_prompt: 1950s Nevada nuclear test desert landscape, a distant mushroom cloud rising on the horizon, soldiers silhouetted in the foreground watching from a trench, documentary military history photography

heading: IN 1983, [NATO](orange) WAR GAMES WERE SO REALISTIC THAT [SOVIET FORCES](orange) WENT TO [NUCLEAR ALERT](red).
body: In **November 1983**, [NATO](orange) conducted **Able Archer 83** — a military exercise simulating escalation to nuclear warfare. Soviet intelligence interpreted the exercises as a possible cover for a real [US](orange) first strike. [Soviet nuclear forces](orange) in [Eastern Europe](orange) [were placed on heightened alert](red). [Soviet](orange) aircraft armed with nuclear weapons were prepared for immediate launch. The crisis passed when the exercises ended. [President Reagan](orange) only learned how close the situation came in **1984** when a [CIA](orange) report was declassified. A **2015 UK government report** concluded the world had come **"closer to nuclear war than was realised at the time."**
photo_prompt: Cold War-era military command bunker interior, radar screens glowing green, uniformed figures at consoles, tension visible in posture, dramatic cold blue and red lighting, documentary military photography

heading: [DRUG COMPANIES](orange) EXTEND THEIR [PATENT MONOPOLIES](red) FOR DECADES. ONE [INSULIN](orange) WAS MODIFIED 74 TIMES.
body: Under US patent law, pharmaceutical companies can [reset their patent clock](red) by making minor modifications to existing drugs — a practice known as **"evergreening."** Modifications can include: a new delivery mechanism, a slightly different molecular form, or a new dosage. [I-MAK](orange) analysis found one insulin product underwent **74 reformulations** over its patent lifetime. The net effect: [generic competitors are blocked from entering the market for decades beyond the original 20-year patent term](red). The [Federal Trade Commission](orange) has identified evergreening as a primary driver of drug price inflation in the US. **Over 70%** of the drugs most commonly prescribed were reformulations of existing products.

heading: A "[COMPLETELY SAFE](red)" MORNING SICKNESS DRUG CAUSED [BIRTH DEFECTS](red) IN OVER [10,000 CHILDREN](orange) WORLDWIDE.
body: In the late **1950s**, the drug [Thalidomide](orange) was marketed across [Europe, Canada, Australia,](orange) and dozens of other countries as a safe treatment for morning sickness and insomnia in pregnant women. The manufacturer, [Grünenthal](orange), advertised it as **"completely safe."** It caused severe limb and organ malformations in an estimated **10,000 to 20,000 children** worldwide, with thousands more miscarried. In the [US](orange), [FDA](orange) medical officer [Dr. Frances Kelsey](orange) repeatedly refused to approve the drug, citing insufficient safety data — a decision that [spared the US from the scale of the crisis seen elsewhere](red). The disaster directly led to the **1962 Kefauver-Harris Amendment**, which created modern US drug safety and efficacy testing requirements.
